barriers.reason: A Thursday 11:30 AM, 4-hour session ends around 3:30 PM, clashing with the 3 PM school pickup; the patient has no one for the kids Thursdays (neighbor works, daughter works until 6:30).
The daughter's downtown schedule until 6:30 leaves no evening backup, so the Thursday chair time conflicts with the family's care coverage.

alternatives.text: Ask the dialysis unit for a later Thursday chair time or a different day that fits school pickup and available rides.
Message the unit social worker for help with caregiving/benefits and to explore Thursday scheduling or transport support.
Discuss a peritoneal or home hemodialysis evaluation as a schedule/transport alternative, noting it requires clinical approval, space, training, and home support.

barriers.reason: The patient eats processed kid-friendly foods (hot dogs, mac and cheese) and relies on what is available at home, so switching to fresh low-potassium produce may be unaffordable or hard to obtain.

alternatives.text: Have the dialysis dietitian redesign the renal diet around foods the patient can actually get and that the children will eat.
Use the Greater Chicago Food Depository locator for pantries open on non-treatment days, then pair selections with renal-dietitian guidance.
Apply through Illinois ABE for income-based SNAP benefits; very low-income households may qualify for expedited benefits within 7 days.
